instruction: Change all body text font size to 44pt on slide 4 and set all image widths to 18cm on slide 5

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Modify body text sizes on slide 4 and image widths on slide 5. Evaluator checks both image dimensions and body text font sizes with proportional partial credit based on percentage of correct elements.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for percentage of correct image widths (18cm), 0.5 for percentage of correct body text font sizes (44pt). Title placeholders are excluded from text checks.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly implements proportional partial credit for both image widths and text font sizes, awarding score based on percentage of matching elements (lines 65, 119).
Body text filtering is properly implemented by excluding title placeholders (placeholder types 1 and 3), which aligns with instruction 'all body text font size' (lines 82-92).
Edge cases are handled correctly: empty slides score 0.0 instead of incorrectly awarding points (lines 37-39, 95-97, 114-116).

Expected values are semantically correct: 44pt font size and 18cm width match instruction requirements.

Minor consideration: Metric only checks text runs with explicit font sizes (run.font.size is not None). If body text inherits font size from paragraph/shape defaults, those runs would be skipped. However, PowerPoint typically sets explicit run-level font sizes when users change formatting, so this is likely acceptable.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider handling inherited font sizes: If a text run doesn't have an explicit font size, could check paragraph or shape-level defaults. However, this may not be necessary given typical PowerPoint editing behavior.
